facts.fact: The World Bank ID4D diagnostic states that the Integrated System for Registry Management (SIGA) was implemented by 2018, enabling digital registration of life events nationwide, and that it now enables the registration of all types of life events (births, deaths, marriages).

The World Bank states that the details of the birth declaration form, completed after a birth and excluding the statistical items, are entered into SIGA digitally and that registration results in immediate issuance of the cedula pessoal with a QR code; no date is given, so the 2023 publication year is used.

The World Bank states that the registration process is conducted digitally via SIGA in DGRN centers, and that SIGA connects to servers hosted in Portugal by the University of Aveiro during registration and document issuance, with no redundancy in the country; no date is given, so the 2023 publication year is used.

The World Bank states that as of 2022 the SIGA database is not comprehensive: it holds birth records from 1920 to 2010, while the stock of paper-based birth records established between 2010 and 2023 and the death, marriage and divorce records still need to be digitized and consolidated.

The World Bank states that SIGA is operational in DGRN centers across the country but not at embassies, and separately that DGRN has 11 centers for all civil registration services plus seven birth registration posts in maternity facilities; it gives no count of the offices entering records in SIGA, and no date, so the 2023 publication year is used.

The World Bank states that DGRN, an autonomous body within the Ministry of Justice, Public Administration and Human Rights, is responsible for civil registration and developed SIGA with its own technicians, while the University of Aveiro in Portugal still maintains, updates and hosts it, which the report calls a key shortcoming; no date is given, so the 2023 publication year is used.

The World Bank states that DGRN had strategic plans for 2017-2019 and 2020-2022 covering all its services but that there is no strategic plan specifically for civil registration and identification; the 2023 publication year is used.

The World Bank states that the digital civil registration system was developed under a 2016 agreement between the government, with INIC, and Camoes, Portugal's Institute for Cooperation and Language, with University of Aveiro support, and that DGRN lacks resources and capacity; no domestic budget line is stated.
